---
title: Model candidates specification
---

`data_models` is a mutable model-selection card after preparation and `obs_resample`.
It reads the JSON catalogue through `estimator_catalogue`. Explicit Commit constructs an unfitted recipe; browsing performs no fitting, installation or automatic model selection. Pure `_analyze`
and `_table` helpers separate requirements from display filters.

Requirements derive from the modeling context and `model_predictors`. Structural
requirements use assigned Sequence/Geometry and repeated Identifier roles. Forecasting
is an explicit exploration control because upstream outcome task and forecasting
objective are distinct. Unknown domain support never passes as compatible.

Default display includes compatible recipes regardless of package availability;
optional controls expose excluded/unreviewed recipes and hide uninstalled packages.
The table supports row selection and filtering. Details include parameters, conditions,
subjective assessments and evidence URLs. Missing evaluation plans remain browsable.
Unsupported types, infinities and empty datasets produce no compatible matches.

Settings persist through standard card configuration. Display-only settings
must not invalidate analysis. Exports return the incoming proxy independently of
settings and table rendering. No extended task or mutable-card commit is necessary.

Acceptance checks cover mixed/missing predictors, roles, survival requirements,
unsupported input, unresolved targets, structural uncertainty, installation filtering,
unchanged data, visible diagnostics and browser table/flip interactions. Catalogue
schema/version/probe checks remain in `tests/test_estimator_catalogue.py`.


The flip-side recipe is a single intrinsic-height, scrolling panel with separate
readiness/evidence badges and responsive section columns. It contains no Notes
output. Data-specific warnings remain on the front; general catalogue and
evaluation caveats are in the card documentation. Compact, narrow and full-screen
layouts must preserve readable headings and access to the final references.


Candidate rows group by estimator ID after per-recipe display filtering. Counts
identify the represented configurations; Type and Summary recipe are not displayed. Summary fields
come from one deterministically ranked recipe; capabilities and evidence are never
merged. Multi-recipe methods expose separate expandable detail panels.

Model taxonomy is stored in catalogue schema 1.4.0, with explicit source mappings
in `taxonomy.json` and static expansion in `model_taxonomy.py`. Five structured
attributes accompany the existing recipe `outputs` list and its `output_review`:
core mechanism, composition, fitting criterion, learning strategy and transparency.
Each classification has values, a review status and a qualification; shared sources
and review date are attached. Capacity growth must remain deferred for stage 2.
New unlisted methods are not classified from name substrings. Preparation-only
entries have a not-applicable predictive taxonomy. Recipe refinements are guarded
by exact configuration and reviewed package version; changed recipes revert to
method-level descriptions and unreviewed output support pending review.

The table exposes six descriptive columns with DataGrid sorting; column filters remain disabled. Its stable
hidden estimator index must survive filtering and sorting. Descriptions are compared
across the displayed recipes: differing labels produce `Varies by recipe`, never a
union of guarantees. The flip side shows the actual recipe descriptions, qualifications
and source links. These descriptions never change compatibility or selectability.
`class_prediction` is normalized to `class_label`; legacy output queries accept both.
Default hinge SGDClassifier and probability-disabled SVC recipes cannot satisfy a
class-probability requirement. Probabilities are not a calibration-quality guarantee.

`build_estimator_catalogue.py --refresh-descriptions` updates the saved snapshot
without importing or fitting estimators and without replacing prior probe evidence.
Normal rebuilds apply the same taxonomy registry. Focused checks cover schema,
refresh reproducibility, source output consistency, changed configuration guards,
component/hybrid distinctions, output support, grouped descriptions and UI selection.

Formulation is removed from the taxonomy and from both card faces. Prediction outputs
summarizes regression recipes as `Point prediction` or `Point prediction & spread`.
Spread requires explicit prediction-specific uncertainty outputs; no inference from
core mechanism, fitting criterion, coefficient errors or ensemble composition is allowed.
A lone quantile remains a point output, with its exact meaning shown in the details.
GaussianProcessRegressor, BayesianRidge and ARDRegression record return_std support;
GPR also records return_cov. The output requirement `prediction_spread` matches any
reviewed spread-output kind. Classification and specialist output distinctions remain.

Learning strategy uses reviewed `eager`, `lazy` or `hybrid` values and separate
configuration-dependent/unreviewed/not-applicable statuses. It describes the predictor,
not routine preprocessing, runtime, data retention or incremental updates. Explicit
method mappings and guarded recipe overrides populate the static JSON; the table
and details use the shared taxonomy labels. Neighbor retrieval is lazy; nearest
centroids, fitted kernels/GPs and trees are eager. Generic wrappers and Cubist with
optional neighbor correction require configuration-specific descriptions. Differing
recipe strategies show `Varies by recipe` without pooling capabilities.

## Estimator commitment

Commit applies the selected method's ranked summary recipe. Construction requires selectable catalogue evidence and a supported preparation adapter. Errors retain the previous commitment. The exported proxy preserves frame, clean_frame, roles and preprocessing and replaces its terminal data_models step. A Learning processing record names the committed model and recipe. No fit occurs. A change to upstream proxy identity invalidates this session commitment. The footer shows the committed estimator independently of row browsing. Predictors are selected before model fitting, preventing target leakage. Commit state is session-local; restoring configuration requires recommitment.
